The standard-library program checked all 77,294 origin-fixed negative supports and all 5,040 seven-point distinct-coordinate order types, and verified nine explicit witnesses by two trace implementations; 1,119 additional small supports were independently cross-checked. Crucially the finite computations are used only after reductions prove they exhaust all unrestricted parameter cases. Empty and full cyclic intervals, coordinate ties, and one-vertex boundaries are treated explicitly.

The 2020 preprint already reports dimension six for unrestricted continuous two-dimensional torus boxes, and the elementary one-dimensional circular-interval boundary is prior knowledge. The finite side-length phase diagram does not follow from either numeric statement without the new matching witnesses and finite obstructions. Accessible primary passages, targeted published-literature searches, and available semantic-record comparisons did not disclose an equivalent finite classification. value.rationale: The classical continuous two-torus VC dimension six does not specify how much finite cyclic-coordinate resolution is needed to retain that shattering power. The result supplies a complete, natural two-parameter classification, locates the sharp asymmetric five-by-six threshold, proves the five-by-five failure and the six-by-six square onset, and describes all thin-grid dimension losses. These exact cutoffs are motivated by the finite sampling of circular-arc boxes and are not arbitrary isolated numerical slices.
